title: Requesting the Secretary of the Interior to authorize unique and one-time arrangements for displays on the National Mall and the Washington Monument during the period beginning on December 31, 2025, and ending on January 5, 2026
official_title: Requesting the Secretary of the Interior to authorize unique and one-time arrangements for displays on the National Mall and the Washington Monument during the period beginning on December 31, 2025, and ending on January 5, 2026.
likelihoodReason: Became Public Law 119-46 on December 2, 2025. Passed the House on November 18, 2025 and the Senate on November 20, 2025.
summary: Asks the Interior Department to allow special one-time displays of 250th-anniversary materials on the National Mall — including projections on the Washington Monument for five nights — around New Year's 2025-2026.
brief: Requests the Interior Secretary authorize one-time 250th-anniversary displays on the National Mall and Washington Monument, December 31, 2025 to January 5, 2026.

top_lines.headline: 250th Anniversary Displays
subs: Requests Interior to allow National Mall displays
Includes 5 nights of projection on the Washington Monument
For the period December 31, 2025 to January 5, 2026

sections.label: Request to the Secretary of the Interior

items.main: Requests the Interior Secretary authorize unique, one-time displays of 250th-anniversary materials on and around the National Mall.
items.detail: Congress requests that the Secretary of the Interior authorize one-time arrangements to display United States semiquincentennial materials, artifacts, digital content, and film footage in and around the National Mall — including projection onto the surface of the Washington Monument for five nights of public display — during the period December 31, 2025 to January 5, 2026, and requests that an enrolled copy be transmitted to the Secretary and the Chair of the United States Semiquincentennial Commission.

gaps: The resolution requests the displays but does not require the Interior Secretary to grant the request.
It authorizes a one-time event window but provides no funding for the displays.
